findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any Detector whose type is metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError instead of evaluating. Previously this handler implemented evaluate and returned an empty list, so process_detectors could skip it safely. The class is a registered GroupType (type_id 8001), so this is a live crash if that slug is ever loaded.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers that follow the docstring will treat the return value as a sequence of results and break (iterating a dict yields keys, not DetectorEvaluationResult objects).

findings.title: Multi-group test builds group_2 expected occurrence with the wrong value
findings.body: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2 the value 10, but the expected IssueOccurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., "group_2", 6, ...). The helper ignores value, so the assertion still passes and never checks that evaluate passes the packet value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. A regression that forwarded the wrong value (or swapped group keys) would not fail this test, and updating the helper to include value would make the test fail for the wrong reason.
